title: On The Origin of Cultural Biases in Language Models: From Pre-training Data to Linguistic Phenomena
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark, CAMeL-2, measures the ability of language models to recognize and appropriately use cultural entities, including religious places (mosques and churches), in different linguistic contexts. It evaluates cultural bias by comparing performance on Arab vs. Western entities in both text-infilling and extractive QA/NER tasks.
findings: Language models demonstrate a significant performance gap favoring Western religious entities (e.g., churches) over Arab religious entities (e.g., mosques) when tested in Arabic. This gap is substantially reduced when the same entities are tested in English. This suggests that the bias stems not just from data representation but from linguistic phenomena like polysemy and tokenization challenges present in the Arabic language.
